claim: WSL2 runs a real Linux kernel with systemd and full syscall compatibility, but uses NAT networking with a changing IP, has no serial-port support, needs usbipd for USB devices, and is slower across the Windows/Linux filesystem boundary.
quote: WSL 2 does not include support for accessing serial ports... WSL 2 uses a Network Address Translation (NAT) service for its virtual network, instead of making it bridged to the host Network Interface Card (NIC) resulting in a unique IP address that will change on restart.

claim: WSL2 blocks kernel modules and low-level hardware access, is slow across /mnt/c, and competes with Windows for RAM via vmmem.
quote: Anything that involves kernel modules, low-level system configuration, or hardware access is either limited or outright blocked. You cannot freely modify the kernel, load arbitrary kernel modules, or experiment with custom boot processes.

claim: Installing Linux to a separate disk makes the rollback trivial — deleting the disk removes the Linux system entirely.
quote: The idea with running Linux on a separate disk is the ability to basically press delete, and the Linux system is gone.

claim: Dual-boot setup requires suspending or decrypting BitLocker before resizing partitions, and disabling Fast Startup because it leaves NTFS volumes hibernated and corruptible when mounted from Linux.
quote: Fast Startup leaves NTFS volumes in a hibernated state and can cause filesystem corruption when Linux mounts them... if BitLocker is enabled, suspend or decrypt it before resizing partitions.

claim: The August 2024 Windows security update applied an SBAT value that made Linux unbootable on dual-boot systems its detection missed.
quote: Verifying shim SBAT data failed: Security Policy Violation. Something has gone seriously wrong: SBAT self-check failed: Security Policy Violation.

claim: Practitioners in a Feb 2026 thread recommend VM first then spare machine, live USB for hardware enumeration, a spare drive for a real trial of days-to-a-week, separate SSDs per OS, and a used mini PC to avoid dual-boot reboot fatigue.
quote: I would strongly recommend playing around with Linux in a virtual machine first, then a spare machine if possible. / I put the live USB in...and it recognized everything. Wifi. Trackpad. Touchscreen. SD card reader. Brightness. / if you have a spare drive to attach, use it and fully install any distro that seems interesting and use it for at least a day or 2, a week if you have the time.

claim: Persistent live USB media cannot reliably update the kernel or regenerate initramfs, which blocks installing proprietary graphics drivers.
quote: When trying to update the kernel (initramfs) on a Ventoy persistent live USB, it produces errors... this prevents installation of graphics card drivers.

claim: GPU passthrough to a VM requires a spare GPU dedicated to the guest and cooperative IOMMU grouping, so a normal VM cannot represent real desktop/GPU performance.
quote: By default, the motherboard's IOMMU groups your GPU with other peripherals... the graphics card will be utilized by the hypervisor to display its operating system console by default, which will block any attempt to detach the graphics card.

claim: Installing Linux to an external SSD leaves the Windows install intact and is a safe way to run Linux full-time.
quote: Installing Linux on an external SSD while leaving your Windows install intact is a safe way to use Linux.

claim: WPF and WinForms have never been ported to Linux or macOS and Microsoft has no announced plans to do so.
quote: WPF and WinForms haven't received official porting to other platforms, and Microsoft currently has no announced plans to do so.

claim: Canonical publishes a searchable list of Ubuntu Certified hardware, usable to check a laptop model before committing.
quote: The 'Ubuntu Certified' label is applied to systems that have been verified and are continuously tested by Canonical throughout the Ubuntu release life cycle.

claim: A live Ubuntu session changes nothing on disk; rebooting without the USB restores the machine exactly.
quote: doesn't alter your computer's configuration in any way, and a simple restart without the USB stick or DVD is all that's needed to restore your machine to its previous state.

claim: WSLg lets Linux GUI applications appear alongside native Windows programs in the Start menu and taskbar.
quote: WSL now supports GUI apps (WSLg), integrating with Windows tooling so that Linux apps appear alongside native Windows programs in the Start menu and taskbar.

claim: CUDA application development is fully supported under WSL2, but developer tooling such as profilers is still preview-only.
quote: CUDA Toolkit support for WSL is still in preview stage as developer tools such as profilers are not available yet, however CUDA application development is fully supported in the WSL2 environment.

claim: Canonical's desktop certification runs over 500 OS-compatibility hardware tests per certified machine.
quote: Canonical's certification team performs an extensive set of over 500 OS compatibility focused hardware tests to ensure the best Ubuntu experience.

claim: When installing to an external SSD, the installer can overwrite the internal EFI partition; disabling internal drives in BIOS before install prevents this.
quote: the EFI partition might be overwritten... This will disconnect your internal storage upon boot so that you won't accidentally overwrite these when you are installing Ubuntu to your external SSD.

claim: A documented 30-day dual-boot Linux trial found days 1-3 smooth, week 1 the friction trough (printer drivers, Bluetooth audio latency, missing apps), and adaptation by week two.
quote: by week two... I stopped fighting Linux and started understanding it.

claim: Linux battery life is often worse than Windows out of the box because OEMs ship Windows drivers with power management precisely tuned to the hardware.
quote: many users find that the battery drains much faster than before... the main reason is that Windows comes pre-installed with optimized drivers specifically designed for the hardware of that laptop model.

claim: TLP tunes low-level Linux power management parameters to improve laptop battery life.
quote: TLP - Optimize Linux Laptop Battery Life

claim: Explicit sync landed in Wayland and eliminated the long-standing NVIDIA flickering and frame-pacing class of bugs.
quote: Wayland integrates explicit sync, eliminating flickering and frame pacing issues with NVIDIA drivers on Linux.

claim: Users report NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM bugchecks on BitLocker-enabled Windows 11 machines dual-booted with Ubuntu.
quote: Bitlocker and dual boot Ubuntu-Windows 11. ERROR NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM

claim: Microsoft took roughly nine months to ship a fix for the SBAT update that broke Linux dual-boot.
quote: 9 Months Later, Microsoft Finally Fixes Linux Dual-Booting Bug

claim: Windows assumes the RTC holds local time while Linux assumes UTC, producing clock skew on dual-boot machines that must be fixed explicitly.
quote: Since systemd version 216, when the RTC is configured to the local time (rather than UTC) systemd will never synchronize back to it, as this might confuse Windows at a later boot.

claim: The reboot required to switch OSes is the practical failure mode of dual-boot: the friction pushes users to stay in one OS.
quote: every time you want to switch between operating systems, you have to stop what you're doing and reboot, which adds up fast.

claim: Dual-booting brings unanticipated pitfalls including unpredictable updates and awkward file sharing between the two systems.
quote: Updates could get a little unpredictable, and even basic things like moving files between systems weren't always as smooth as you'd expect.

claim: A dual-booter kept an 800 GB Windows partition and never booted into it once after installing Linux.
quote: I haven't booted into Windows since the day I installed Linux, not once... an 800GB Windows partition that just sits there.

claim: In January 2026 Xe Iaso reported not having booted Windows on their tower in over three months, and planned to move to Fedora.
quote: I haven't booted into Windows in over 3 months on my tower.

claim: The '2026 will be my year of the Linux desktop' post drew 835 points and 639 comments on Hacker News in January 2026, showing the topic remains actively contested.
quote: 2026 will be my year of the Linux desktop — 835 points, 639 comments

claim: JetBrains Rider supports .NET, ASP.NET, MAUI, Blazor and Azure development on Linux.
quote: Rider supports developing .NET, ASP.NET, MAUI, Blazor, and Azure applications on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

claim: Windows 10 reached end of support on 14 October 2025 and shed 9.4 points of share between then and June 2026.
quote: Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025... Between the October 2025 deadline and June 2026, Windows 10 shed another 9.4 points of share.

claim: Desktop Linux rose from 2.76% in July 2022 to about 4.7% in 2025 and is projected near 6% by late 2026.
quote: Desktop Linux climbed from 2.76% in July 2022 to 4.7% in 2025, a rise of about 70% in three years, and is projected near 6% by late 2026.
